correctness.rationale: For fixed odd \(N\ge5\) with nonzero edge weights, unitarity gives the uniform invariant law. The shortest walk between a distance-\(d\) vertex pair has amplitude coefficient A_{j,d}/d!, fixing \(P\sim(A_{j,d}/d!)^2\tau^{2d}\). Any nonzero coefficient of odd degree below \(N\) in P_uv−P_vu would define an odd closed walk shorter than the chordless odd cycle, impossible. At degree \(N\), complementary clockwise/counterclockwise arcs give signed coefficient \(4(-1)^{m+d+1}(\prod_j a_j)\sin\Phi/[d!(N-d)!]\). Pair entropy is \(\Delta^2/P\) to leading order; exponent \(2N-2d\) reaches its unique minimum \(N+1\) at \(d=m\), yielding the long-arc squared hopping formula. Exact evenness of total entropy eliminates the odd correction, giving \(O(\tau^{N+3})\). A valid sign and normalization cross-check used exact rational matrix-power computations for \(N=3,5,7,9\) (328 identities), and independent matrix exponential entropy diagnostics (19 tests). These finite experiments corroborate the arbitrary-\(N\) proof rather than establishing it.

value.rationale: In a physically motivated monitored magnetic walk, stationary entropy production directly quantifies broken detailed balance even though stationary populations remain uniform. The theorem reveals a counterintuitive mechanism: rare maximal-distance transitions, not common nearest-neighbor hops, determine the first irreversible term. This requires exact graph-path interference, distance-dependent probability denominators, and coupling-sensitive long-arc products; the resulting \(N+1\) exponent quantifies ring-size suppression and suggests experimental sampling resolution. It is a general structural law for every odd ring with arbitrary positive edge magnitudes, not a specially chosen numerical case.
